context_requirements: Active HCV replication or HCV-derived viral proteins/RNA; none of the nine lines are HCV-infected or express HCV replicons

For host-directed antivirals (e.g., mTOR inhibitors, cyclophilins, NS5A inhibitors), the relevant host pathway must be engaged; at 10 µM in uninfected cells these agents produce only generic cytostatic/cytotoxic effects
falsifiers: Reproducible, concentration-dependent and class-specific transcriptional signature at 6 h in uninfected cell lines
Shared gene-expression changes across multiple mechanistically distinct HCV inhibitors that are absent for non-antiviral drugs at matched cytotoxicity

evidence.supports: mTOR-inhibitor drugs reported to suppress HCV replication and induce apoptosis/proliferation changes in HepG2 cells, but effects were generic cytotoxicity/apoptosis rather than a specific HCV transcriptional program
